memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Command the Israelites to send away from the camp anyone who has a defiling skin disease or a discharge of any kind, or who is ceremonially unclean because of a dead body. Send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them." - Num 5:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives instructions about keeping the camp clean, sending outside those who were ceremonially unclean. Before we misunderstand this, we must be clear: "unclean" here does not mean sinful or worthless. It was a ceremonial state, not a moral judgment. These were not bad people being punished; they were people temporarily set apart under the old covenant system.

The reason God gives is striking: "where I dwell among them." The holiness of the camp mattered because God Himself lived in its midst. His presence was the whole point. A holy God dwelling among His people meant that holiness had to be taken seriously.

These ceremonial laws are not binding on believers today. The New Testament makes clear that such external cleanness has been fulfilled and set aside in Christ (Col 2:16-17; Mark 7:19). We are no longer sent outside a physical camp for these things.

But the deeper truth remains gloriously true: God dwells among His people, and now, by His Spirit, within them. What the old covenant pictured through an external camp, the new covenant fulfils inwardly. Through Christ, we who were once "outside" have been brought near (Eph 2:13).

Rejoice today that the holy God who once dwelt in a camp now dwells in you by His Spirit.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What does it mean that God chooses to dwell among His people?
- How does it comfort you that in Christ you are brought near, not sent away?
- How can you honour God's presence within you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ I am brought near, never sent away. Help me to honour Your holy presence that now dwells within me. Amen.
